Organizer set O, my independent 3D-bbox scorer (1 m tolerance): inside STOP-matched frames 383 -> 416 of 801 (team: 384 -> 411); 8/8 inside objects STOPped; edge cube #4 2 -> 18 frames, first STOP 5.2 -> 35.0 m; edge box #6 6 -> 13 frames, first STOP 10.3 -> 24.2 m; background false STOP frames at 129-141 m 3 -> 0; outside box #7 still 8 false STOP frames at 129-142 m (unchanged). safety_concerns: Learned opinion (tracking.doubt_*): a track the rules would STOP beyond 25 m can be held as advisory for up to 10 matched frames (about 1 s, about 17 m at 17 m/s). This was observed on an organizer object (set O #6: 28.7 -> 24.7 m). The threshold is the highest that delays none of 102 synthetic positives, i.e. zero margin; a 2x margin (0.0111) was measured by the team but not shipped.

Far-evidence approach gate (thin_far_min_distance 60, weak_min_points 4): a track ever matched by a far scan line or weak cluster is not reported at all (neither STOP nor advisory) unless its range decreases linearly at >= 2 m/s. The flag is sticky for the life of the track. tests/test_far_thin.py asserts that a standing object with 8 full in-envelope hits after one scan-line hit is never reported. A standing or creeping train, or an object moving away from the train, could be silenced.

gauge.reference 2 relies on the organizers' placement frame. Within 60 m on straight track the strict envelope shifts up to 0.2 m toward the sensor axis, so an object up to 0.2 m inside the rail envelope on one side is CAUTION instead of STOP until nearer, and there is a step of up to 0.2 m at 60 m. criteria.name: Functionality (working solution)
reasons: Verified from raw per-frame outputs (/data/work/base/gate vs /data/work/final2/gate) and the gate JSON (docs/evidence/results/regression_gate_2026-09-27_quality.json, commit 25498c1; no detector change up to 8b74cd0; the seal verifies): full gate PASS against P3d with 0 gated metrics worse. The ride goes from 45/38/183 to 21/22/85 events/episodes/frames. The five empty bags go from 13/16/58 to 9/8/31. 127 of 241 old alarm frames are gone and exactly 2 are new (new_data_5 at 95.7 m, new_data_6 at 118.4 m), as claimed.

The one real obstacle recording still works: doubleT_obstacle person 61/61, rail object 125/126, 0 FP events. Set O: 411/801 in-envelope STOP frames, background 0, GO overclaims 46 to 16. History stress 78 to 49 events; captured node histories 2 to 0.

The false-alarm gains are in-sample and come mostly from the learned opinion. With the opinion alone the ride is 24/28/109 (screens/p2ride_c1.json). My quick screen with tracking.doubt_extra_hits=0 gives five empty 13/16/56 and set O background 3, so all of the five-bag and background gain is the opinion, whose negatives are those same recordings. With the 2x-margin threshold 0.0111 the ride keeps 36 events (track_opinion_threshold_ride.txt).

Safety regression 1, the sensor-axis envelope (gauge.reference 2). I injected a person on the ride (far_range_eval, 6 files, centre 1.05 m from the rail axis, about 0.25 m inside the rails' envelope). Right side, shipped: STOP in 24/91 frames at 30-60 m and 55/68 at 0-30 m. The same config with reference 0: 91/91 and 67/68. Left side: unchanged at 91/91 and 68/68.

Safety regression 2, far evidence. Set F box1.0 at lateral 0.38 loses its STOP from 85.3 m to 72.9 m; it resumes only at 70.8 m. The ablation thin_far_min_distance=0 plus weak_min_points=0 restores the hits. Traced mechanism: the box cluster joined a track started by a bed scan line (far_evidence is sticky), and the 5-hit approach fit then failed.

Safety regression 3, standing or creeping train. At the tracker level with shipped defaults, one 4-voxel weak hit at 75 m followed by dense in-envelope clusters is never reported, not even advisory. This holds for a person walking to a standing train (75 to 5 m) and for a train creeping at 1.5 m/s; with far evidence off it is a STOP at about 74 m. tests/test_far_thin.py codifies this behaviour.
The opinion delays set O #6 (big_edge_inside): track 201 is withheld as 'doubt' at 28.66 m in frames 569-570 and is STOPped only at 24.68 m. With the opinion off, my quick screen STOPs it at 28.66 m.
missing: No real-obstacle data from a moving train. All range and positive evidence beyond doubleT_obstacle (a standing train, 55 m) is synthetic.

The regressions above need fixing: an envelope from the rails or a union rather than a side shift; far_evidence that does not contaminate dense tracks and does not suppress at low approach speed; an opinion threshold with a margin.
Advisory CAUTION is still on 27-69% of frames of the empty bags (README table).

criteria.name: Generalization
reasons: Good: the core is tunnel geometry plus rails, envelope and anomaly logic, as the spec encourages. The opinion uses grouped CV by ride piece (held-out AUC 0.9738, report verified). The placement study was pre-registered on seen organizer shapes at new places and backgrounds (544 to 723, controls 0). The team labels its in-sample numbers.

gauge.reference 2 adopts the organizers' placement frame, not the rails. In set O both 'inside edge' objects are on the + side with negative rail-frame gauge margins (#4 -0.01 m, #6 -0.09 m), and the 'outside near' cube is +0.065 m inside the rails' envelope on the - side. The shift is fitted to that single configuration and to this rig's yaw sign.

Its premise 'rails at -0.25 +- 0.03 deg to the sensor axis on every recording' is false. doubleT_obstacle has a median of -1.16 deg on straight-flagged frames (my read of base gate outputs; per-frame p10-p90 spread is 0.2-1.3 deg), so there the clamp is active from about 10 m.

The real-person gain on doubleT_obstacle (58 to 61, first alarm frame 11 to 8) is entirely this shift: my quick screen with gauge.reference=0 gives 58 and frame 11. The person enters from the + side, which gains 0.2 m.

Several rules are sized to single set O objects or single captures: floating_free_max_dy 0.95 to 1.2 for #4; weak_min_points 4 for the cube's 4 voxels; column_width_trim / min_cut 0.25 for the one 26.09 clear-run cluster (0.69 m body in a 1.10 m box).
The opinion threshold 0.0222 is the highest that delays no held-out synthetic positive, so it sits at the edge of the positives. It was chosen on those same held-out rows.
missing: Organizer answer to Q1, or a rail-based envelope with a symmetric safety union.
Positives from a new rig or yaw.
An opinion threshold with margin validated on truly unseen positives.
Rules not dimensioned to individual set O objects.

claims_found_wrong_or_overstated: QUALITY_CYCLE_2026-09-27.md: 'Set O, doubleT_obstacle and 10 synthetic crossing persons ... 0 onsets delayed'. Wrong: the opinion withheld set O #6 ('doubt', 28.66 m, frames 569-570), and it STOPped only at 24.68 m. The simulation counts only scorer-matched rows.
The cycle doc and README say '#6 ... its track STOPs from ~28 m'. In the shipped config the track STOPs from 24.7 m; 28.7 m holds only without the opinion.

'On every recording the rails run at -0.25 +- 0.03 deg to the sensor axis on straight track (0.2 m at 50 m)'. doubleT_obstacle is -1.16 deg (center_y(45 m) about -1.0 m), and the per-frame spread is far larger than 0.03 deg.
Set F straight 'identical detection'. box1.0 recall at 50-100 m went from 125/133 to 119/133 (a STOP gap from 85.3 to 72.9 m) because of far evidence; the gate does not gate this row.

Limits: the sensor-axis reference makes an object up to 0.2 m inside 'between ~45 and 60 m' CAUTION until nearer. My injected person, about 0.25 m inside on the losing side, is STOP in only 24/91 frames at 30-60 m and 55/68 at 0-30 m (91/91 and 67/68 from the rails).

The real-person improvement on doubleT_obstacle (58 to 61 of 61, first alarm frame 11 to 8) is presented as a detection gain. It comes entirely from shifting the envelope 0.2 m towards the side the person enters from (reference=0 gives 58 and frame 11).
The five-empty and set O background FP gains (13/16 to 9/8; background 3 to 0) come entirely from the opinion, whose negatives were trained on those same recordings. This is in-sample.
README headline table is stale and contradicts its own cycle summary: five empty bags '13 events, 58 alarm frames, 16 STOP episodes' and crossing person '58 of 61, first alarm frame 11'.

Config and docstring comments describe shipped-on features as 'off by default', 'opt-in' or 'experiment' (e.g. gate_along_only: true '# (P4 history, off)'). The floating_free_max_dy comment ('inside the 1.05 m envelope edge') contradicts its new value of 1.2.
The committed bench_native.txt shows a 3519.8 ms tracking frame (pre-fix) and was not re-measured after the 25498c1 fix; the CHANGELOG entry for the cycle is uncommitted at 8b74cd0.
safety_concerns: gauge.reference 2 narrows the strict envelope by up to 0.2 m on one side within 60 m and widens it on the other. The losing side depends on the rig's yaw sign. Measured on shipped code: a person about 0.25 m inside the rails' envelope on the right is STOPped at 90 m (beyond 60 m) and then drops to CAUTION at 30-60 m (24/91 STOP frames).

Far evidence. far_evidence is sticky and is inherited when a dense object cluster associates with a track started by a bed or vault scan line. The track then needs a clean 5-hit approach fit before a STOP: a set F 1 m box in mid-track lost its STOP from 85.3 to 70.8 m.

Far evidence at a standing or slow train (<2 m/s approach): a track that ever had a weak or scan-line hit beyond 60 m is never reported at all, not even advisory, as a person walks up to a standing train or a train creeps at 1.5 m/s. This is codified in the tests and absent from the Limits.

The learned opinion withholds STOP onsets beyond 25 m for 10 matched frames. The count resets if the rule zone flickers, and misses do not advance it, so the delay can exceed 1 s. Its threshold sits at the edge of the held-out positives, and it already delayed an organizer in-envelope object by about 4 m.

column_width_trim extends the column demotion (tall and narrow means advisory) to clusters with a box width of 1.0-1.35 m and sparse tails. The rule is sized to one captured cluster; the added risk is small but real for tall irregular objects.
fastest_points_to_gain: Replace the one-sided gauge.reference with a union of the rail and sensor-axis envelopes near the train, or keep the rails. Add a side-symmetric edge-object regression test, and gate STOP frames per distance bin for both sides.

Stop far_evidence from contaminating dense tracks: clear the flag once a normal in-envelope cluster matches, and never block a track whose hits are all clean. Allow a report without the approach condition at a standing train once dense hits exist. Gate the set F recall_by_bin.
Give the opinion threshold a safety margin (0.0111 or lower), and count per-frame 'doubt' onsets on labelled objects rather than only scorer-matched rows.

Correct the overstated claims: the 0 onsets delayed, the #6 '~28 m', the every-recording yaw, set F 'identical', the extent of the edge regression, and the standing-train limit. Refresh the README headline table and the stale comments. Re-run and commit bench_native.txt after the fix.
